    AI Overview
    Gary Woodland is a 2019 U.S. Open champion who made an emotional comeback to win the 2026 Houston Open after undergoing brain surgery in September 2023 to remove a tumor, which was followed by a challenging battle with PTSD and intense anxiety. Despite struggling to return to form in 2024, Woodland has continued to compete, aiming to inspire others to "just keep fighting". 
    Brain Tumor and Surgery (2023) 
    • Diagnosis: In August 2023, Woodland announced he had a lesion on his brain. The tumor was pressing on the part of his brain that controls fear and anxiety, creating significant, unprovoked anxiety symptoms.
    • Surgery: He underwent successful surgery to remove the tumor in September 2023.
    • Fear of Death: Before the surgery, Woodland wrote letters to his wife and children, fearing he might not survive. 
    Battle with PTSD (2024–2025) 
    • Hidden Struggle: Although he returned to the PGA Tour in January 2024, Woodland admitted to dealing with intense, hidden anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), stating he felt like he was "dying inside" while trying to live a normal life on tour.
    • Physical Symptoms: He suffered from intense hypervigilance, where strangers approaching from behind would trigger panic, and at times suffered from blurred vision during competition.
    • Missed Cuts: He struggled on the course in 2024, missing 11 of 26 cuts and finishing 155th in the FedExCup, but refused to stop competing. 
    Triumphant Return (2026) 
    • Houston Open Victory: In March 2026, Woodland won the Texas Children’s Houston Open for his first victory since the 2019 U.S. Open.
    • Emotional Win: He finished 21 under at Memorial Park, winning by five shots and breaking down in tears after his final putt, embracing his wife and team.
    • Message of Hope: Woodland expressed immense gratitude to his supporters and dedicated his comeback to anyone struggling, proving he could overcome the "invisible battle" of PTSD. 
    Before his health struggles, Woodland was recognized as one of the toughest competitors on the PGA Tour, with a signature victory at the 2019 U.S. Open at Pebble Beach.

    AI Overview
    Gary Woodland
    underwent successful brain surgery in September 2023 to remove a lesion that was causing severe anxiety and fear. Following his recovery, he was diagnosed with PTSD, yet he returned to the PGA Tour in January 2024 and achieved an emotional victory at the 2026 Houston Open. 
    Key Details Regarding Gary Woodland: 
    • The Health Crisis: In 2023, Woodland was diagnosed with a lesion on his brain that was affecting the area controlling fear and anxiety.
    • Surgery: On September 19, 2023, he underwent surgery to remove the tumor. Surgeons had to remove part of the lesion, but left some to prevent potential loss of sight or motor function.
    • Post-Surgery Challenges:
      Following the surgery, Woodland struggled with intense anxiety, PTSD, and a fear of dying, which significantly impacted his life and game.
    • Return to Golf: He returned to competition in January 2024 but struggled with his game throughout the year, missing 11 of 26 cuts.
    • 2026 Comeback: In March 2026, Woodland opened up about his ongoing battle with PTSD and followed it with an emotional win at the Texas Children’s Houston Open, his first victory since 2019.
